CLINICAL INFORMATION:
Known case of Multiple Sclerosis. Presented with intermittent neurological symptoms for follow-up_
MRI BRAIN FINDINGS:
Multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions are noted in the periventricular white matter; juxtacortical
regions, and callososeptal interface: Some of the lesions show ovoid morphology, oriented
perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, consistent with demyelinating plaques_
There is no definite diffusion restriction_
No associated mass effect or midline shift is seen.
The corpus callosum shows focal areas of signal abnormality: The infratentorial region demonstrates
few small hyperintense foci in the cerebellar white matter and brainstem:
Post-contrast images show no significant abnormal enhancement:
The ventricles are normal in size and configuration. No hydrocephalus is seen. The major intracranial
vessels demonstrate normal
voids
No evidence of acute hemorrhage or extra-axial collection is noted:
IMPRESSION:
Multiple hyperintense demyelinating plaques in periventricular; juxtacortical, callososeptal,
infratentorial regions, in keeping with Multiple Sclerosis.
No enhancing lesion is seen
3_
No acute intracranial abnormality:
Correlation with clinical and previous imaging is advised

CLINICAL INFORMATION:
~standing clinical depression
2 years
with recent complaints of persistent low mood,
poor concentration and memory difficulties. Rule out neuropsychiatric sequelae.
MRI FINDINGS:
Brain parenchyma shows no evidence of acute infarct; hemorrhage O mass lesion.
Mild diffuse cerebral atrophy is noted, predominantly in the frontal and temporal lobes,
with mild prominence of the ventricular system and cortical sulci.
FLAIR images demonstrate subtle hyperintensities in the periventricular white matter;
likely representing chronic microvascular changes.
No abnormal enhancement is seen post-contrast.
MR
Spectroscopy (single voxel, left frontal region) shows reduced NAA/Cr ratio (1.2;
normal ~1.6-2.0) with relative increase in choline (Cho/Cr: 1.4), suggestive of neuronal
dysfunction, which can be seen in chronic depression
No evidence of demyelinating plaques Or other focal pathology:
IMPRESSION:
Mild cerebral atrophy with subtle periventricular white matter changes, likely related to
chronic depressive disorder:
MR Spectroscopy findings suggest neuronal dysfunction with reduced NAA and
increased choline, consistent with long-term clinical depression:
No evidence of acute intracranial pathology:
Correlation with clinical findings is advised
